_roadWidth: 62.0, RE-DERIVED FROM THE PAINTING by tools/trace_level5.py, not taken from a geometry file -- level 5's plate arrived on its own, unlike levels 3 and 4. Normals are cast through the painted track from each lane's centreline and the median taken per lane, and the NARROWEST lane's median is the answer, because the road has to fit its tightest stretch. The four arms are not the same width: west 62, east 64, north 74, south 90. THE JUNCTION IS EXCLUDED FROM THAT MEASUREMENT and has to be: four roads meeting is 150 px of paint across, and a handful of those samples drags a short arm's median right up -- the south arm read 85 before that exclusion existed and 90 after the trace was refined, which is the arm genuinely being wide rather than the junction leaking in. 62 is WIDER than level 4's 50 and level 3's 54.6, so the hero and the line have more room here than on either.
note:
THE CROSSROADS, and the first map in the game with more than two gates. Every coordinate comes from tools/trace_level5.py, which classifies the plate, takes the largest connected run of road, and walks a geodesic down the MIDDLE of the painted band from each edge opening to the junction. Nothing here was traced by eye. Re-derive it with `python3 tools/trace_level5.py --overlay tools/L5_pads_overlay.png` and LOOK AT THE OVERLAY as well as the numbers.
THE PLATE IS NOT THE SHAPE THE BRIEF DESCRIBED, and this is the single most important thing to know about this file. The brief asked for two roads in from the left and two out to the right. The painting has FOUR ARMS: one road in from the west, one down from the north, one up from the south, and ONE out to the east through a gap in the castle wall. Each edge is touched by the road exactly once -- west at y 296-362, north at x 457-529, south at x 480-581, east at y 352-419 -- and the right-hand arm was checked at full resolution before this was written, because a second exit would have been the level's signature. There is one road east. So level 5 is THREE GATES AND ONE EXIT: the three western arms are all on the night side of the seam, they converge at the crossroads, and everything leaves through the castle gap.
THE MAP IS CENTRE-LOADED, which is the opposite of level 4. Fourteen pads sit around the junction and 85.4% of the whole route is inside some pad's range, against level 4's 45.3% of its tail. That is the terrain: the ground beside all four arms takes a tower, and the brief asked for the crossroads to be contestable from both halves.
_spotRadius: 34, every other level's, and for the same reason level 3 records: world 1280 renders to 844 CSS px, so 34 world px is a 44.8 px tap diameter and anything under 44 pt is smaller than a thumb. Two pads need 2 x spotRadius between centres before their tap targets overlap, so 34 needs 68 -- and the closest pair here is 68.15 px. That is the tightest of the five levels, by 6 px less margin than level 4's 74.11, and it is the placer running right up against its own constraint rather than a coincidence.
_waypoints:
THE EXIT ARM, east from the crossroads to the gap in the castle wall, and it is the lane called `main`. It is the trunk every enemy finishes on, so it is the one lane that reaches an exit, exactly as level 3's and level 4's shared tails are.
WAYPOINT 0 IS THE JUNCTION, to 0.00 px, because the three gates all merge into it at index 0 and a merge point that is not shared is a sideways step at the join. Its LAST point is not traced: a gateway is appended 60 px along the line the arm is already travelling as it leaves the plate at x=1279, so enemies walk off the board rather than vanishing at its edge. That is how levels 2, 3 and 4 do it and for the reason level 2 records -- dragging the final traced point out instead would swing the closing segment off the paint.
_lanes:
THREE GATES, ONE EXIT. All three run in from the night side and merge into the trunk at its waypoint 0. Two edits per lane, both documented rather than silent, and both the ones level 4 records: a gateway point is prepended ON THE LINE OF THAT ARM'S FIRST TRACED SEGMENT rather than level with the opening, so an enemy walks in along the road it is already on; and each arm's last traced point is snapped onto the junction, since a branch has to END at the join.
THE THREE ROUTES ARE NOT THE SAME LENGTH AND CANNOT BE MADE SO. West walks 1436.4 px gate to exit, south 1217.3 and north 1170.1 -- a 22.7% spread. Levels 3 and 4 have equal routes and their wave tables lean on it: groups released from both gates on the same delay ARRIVE TOGETHER, which is what makes a split wave a two-front problem rather than a queue. Here that is a property of the painting, not of a choice: the north arm is 392 px of road and the west arm is 662, and the only way to equalise them would be to push the north gateway 269 px further off the plate, which is seven seconds of a Thrall walking where nobody can see it. So the arrival times are equalised in the WAVE TABLE instead, with per-group delays, and waves.level5.json's `_arrival` carries the numbers. THE WEST GATE IS THE SLOW ONE and the north gate is the fast one, by 266 px -- about 3.6 seconds at a Glider's speed.
EVERY ROUTE HERE IS SHORT. The longest is 1436.4 against level 4's 1479, level 3's 1560 and level 1's 1977, and the shortest is 1170. A point of enemy health therefore buys more on this level than on any before it, which is why its wave table is not level 4's with the names changed.
_buildSpots:
FOURTEEN PADS, matching levels 2, 3 and 4 (15, 15 and 14), placed by tools/trace_level5.py and verified by tools/check_level5.py on the four properties level 3 established. ON GROUND: each pad's 24 px core sits on ground the classifier calls turf -- the graveyard's indigo or the meadow's green -- and clear of every crypt, tombstone, railing, dead tree, fir, rock, bush, pumpkin, wall and banner. IN RANGE: each pad is 46 to 110 px from the nearest lane centreline against a tower range of 112. APART: the closest pair is 68.15 px, over the 68 that spotRadius needs. AND BOTH HALVES REACH THE MIDDLE: eight pads sit on the night ground and six on the day ground, and each half was given a floor of four pads within 260 px of the junction BEFORE anything competed for the remaining slots. That last one is not decoration -- a single greedy sweep ordered by distance to the junction puts all fourteen on the meadow, because the meadow has the more open ground beside it, and the crossroads stops being contestable from the graveyard at all.
WHAT THE PADS COVER: 85.4% of the whole route is inside some pad's range -- west 81.0%, east 77.6%, north 100%, south 93.2%. Level 4 covers 45.3% of its tail and is won or lost before the merge. This one is the other shape: the fight is AT the crossroads, and a wave that gets through the middle is very nearly gone.
